Project /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23 (Node 22, node:test, built-ins only). Apply this review fix list to the server test files. Do NOT touch server.mjs, public/, or test/helpers/server-harness.mjs (already updated by me — read it first: it now exports `assertError(res, status, message, label?)`, `stopServer(child)` (SIGKILL + await 'close'), `chunkedPost(port, pieces: Buffer[], headers?)` resolving {status, headers, text, json}, `JSON_HEADERS`; `startServer` now has its own timeout). Keep every test's meaning and every case exactly as strong as now (same inputs, same exact expected values); this is refactoring plus labels only. No console.log; functions < 50 lines.

Fixes:
1. test/server.rules.test.mjs: delete local `expectError` (around line 21) and use harness `assertError(res, status, msg, label)` everywhere with the same labels. Delete local `chunkedPost` (around line 45) and use the harness `chunkedPost(port, pieces)` (split the payload into the same number of Buffer pieces as now). Build the 10001-byte bodies at ~:111, :119, :131 with the existing `sizedBody` helper instead of hand padding (if sizedBody can't express a case, leave it). Write invisible / non-ASCII-whitespace characters in string literals as \u escapes (e.g. '﻿hi ', '​', '　hi ', 'x�', full-width digits may stay literal but whitespace-like chars must be escapes) — around :185, :212, :224 and anywhere else.
2. test/server.routing.test.mjs: delete local `chunkedUpload` (~:143-168) and use harness `chunkedPost(port, Array.from({length: 32}, () => Buffer.alloc(65536, 0x61)))` (2 MB chunked, expect 413 'body too large' via assertError with label). Pass labels to every assertError in loops: at ~:47 `${method} ${p}`, ~:74 `p`, ~:88 `name` (on the non-HEAD branch too), ~:240 a label. Replace the inline kill+wait at ~:221-222 with `await stopServer(first.child)`.
3. test/server.startup.test.mjs: replace local `waitExit` (~:18) with harness `stopServer`. `assertOneLine(stderr, label)` takes a label and every message includes it; pass the PORT value label at ~:38. Use harness JSON_HEADERS instead of local `json` (~:92). Replace the fixed 100 ms sleep (~:101) with `await stopServer(srv.child)` and then assert `out()` exactly equals the listening line (stopServer waits for 'close', so all stdout is drained).
4. test/server.datafile.test.mjs: use harness JSON_HEADERS instead of `JSON_H` (~:16). Extract `assertRejected(res, name, label)` doing the three asserts (code 1, stdout '', stderr exactly `cannot read data file ${name}\n`) and use it at ~:52-54, :64-66, :78-80 (and the 'extra top-level key' test, and the echo test where name = the shown name). Replace the `restart` kill/wait (~:185) with harness `stopServer`. Drop the assertion on the file's internal `nextId` (~:199) — the layout is free; keep the restart-based id checks. Rename `a`/`b`/`f`/`g` (~:91-107) to `emptyServer`/`seededServer`/`emptyFile`/`seededFile`.

Then run: `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23 && node --test test/server.rules.test.mjs test/server.routing.test.mjs test/server.startup.test.mjs test/server.datafile.test.mjs` (if Bash is denied, say so; do not try workarounds). Report what changed per file and the pass/fail counts.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

schema.name: Read
schema.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

schema.name: Write
schema.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

schema.name: Edit
schema.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git

schema.name: Bash
schema.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

All four test files are edited, but I couldn't run any tests. Bash was denied in this session, so there are no pass/fail counts. I didn't try a workaround.

You'll need to run `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23 && node --test test/server.rules.test.mjs test/server.routing.test.mjs test/server.startup.test.mjs test/server.datafile.test.mjs` yourself.

**`test/server.rules.test.mjs`**
- The local `expectError` and local `chunkedPost` are gone. Every call now uses the harness `assertError` with the same labels.
- `chunkedPost` goes through the harness version. A new `inThirds(buf)` helper splits the payload into three Buffers, the same split as before. The 10001-byte chunked case now uses `assertError(..., 413, MSG.big, 'chunked 10001')`.
- The 10001-byte bodies at ~:111 and ~:131 now come from `sizedBody(10001, false)`.
- The body at ~:119 stays hand-built. It is 9990 characters with no space padding, which `sizedBody` can't express.
- Whitespace-like and invisible characters in string literals are now `\u` escapes: `\u3000`, `\uFEFF`, `\u200B` and `\uFFFD`.
- I also escaped `é` as `\u00e9` in two places. Emoji, full-width digits and Arabic digits stay literal.
- `http` and the unused local assert helper are removed from the imports.
- I rewrote the whole file to get the escapes in, because my edit tool kept treating the escapes as identical to the literal characters. I read the file back in full beforehand and kept every case and expected value. A diff against git would confirm that.

**`test/server.routing.test.mjs`**
- The local `chunkedUpload` is removed. The test now sends 32 pieces of 65536 `0x61` bytes through the harness `chunkedPost` and checks 413 `'body too large'` with `assertError`, labelled `'chunked 2 MB'`.
- Labels added to the `assertError` calls: `${method} ${p}` at :47, `p` at :74, `name` at :88 (the non-HEAD branch), and labels on the 405 and DELETE cases.
- The 500 checks are labelled `'DELETE with save failing'` and `'POST with save failing'`.
- The concurrent-DELETE loop is labelled `` `concurrent DELETE #${i}` ``, and still asserts only the 404 results.
- The kill and wait at ~:221 is now `await stopServer(first.child)`.
- Imports: dropped `http`, added `stopServer` and `chunkedPost`.

**`test/server.startup.test.mjs`**
- The local `waitExit` is removed, and `stopServer` replaces its use in the default-port test.
- `assertOneLine(stderr, label)` now puts the label in every message. It gets the `PORT=...` label at ~:38 and `'port in use'` in the port-in-use test, whose other asserts are labelled too.
- The local `json` is replaced by `JSON_HEADERS`.
- The 100 ms sleep is replaced by `await stopServer(srv.child)`, followed by the existing exact assert that `out()` equals the listening line.
- Two `assertError` calls got labels.

**`test/server.datafile.test.mjs`**
- `JSON_H` is replaced by `JSON_HEADERS`.
- New `assertRejected(res, name, label)` does the three asserts: code 1, empty stdout, and stderr exactly `cannot read data file ${name}\n`. It's used in the rejected-files loop, the extra-top-level-key test, the rejected-paths test, and the echo test (with `shown` as the name). The echo test previously didn't check stdout, so it now does. That's one assertion stronger than before.
- `restart` now uses `stopServer`.
- The assertion on the file's internal `nextId` is dropped, along with the `f` variable it used. The restart-based id checks stay.
- `a`/`b`/`f`/`g` in 'valid files load' are renamed to `emptyServer`/`seededServer`/`emptyFile`/`seededFile`.

I found nothing unclear in the spec.
